item.name: 0. Start here
item.description: The `auth` tag, in the order to run it. 1) `login` with `{{username}}` / `{{password}}` (sets the session + CSRF cookies; the test script stores `csrfToken`). 2) `getIdentity` — check `mustRotate` and the permission list. 3) If `mustRotate` is true (the bootstrap admin always starts that way) run `rotateOwnCredential`: until then every other route answers `428 MUST_ROTATE`. After a rotation set the environment `password` to the new credential. 4) `logout` when done. See the README for the cookie-jar notes.

item.name: login · Establish a session

header.description: Non-browser clients must send a trusted Origin on every state-changing request (login included). Must equal an entry of sm.gateway.trusted-origins.

description.content:
operationId: `login`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/cp/auth/login`

**Establish a session**

Establishes the session, so it requires no verb. A login is
`(organization, username, credential)` (`OR-125` (4)): a username is unique
*per organization*, so two organizations may each have an `operator`.
`organization` is the organization's id (a UUID) or its name, compared
without regard to case, taken as typed (surrounding whitespace is a `400`,
never trimmed). The username is compared without regard to case too; the
case folding is PostgreSQL's `lower()` under the database's locale, so a
database created with the `C`/`POSIX` locale folds ASCII letters only (a
UTF-8 locale is required for non-ASCII folding: `docs/runbooks/install-prerequisites.md`).

**`organization` is OPTIONAL** (`OR-131` Q3). Omitted, it is the install's
only organization when the install holds exactly one; when it holds several
an omitted `organization` is `400 BAD_REQUEST` (the owner accepted that
this reveals that more than one exists), raised before any credential work.
⚠️ An organization that is NAMED and does not exist is refused
**exactly as a wrong credential is** (`401 AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`, the same
body, the same work, including the same number of database statements, the
same throttle and audit record), so a login cannot be used to learn which
organizations exist. An `organization` that is present but empty, over 256 characters or
padded with whitespace is a malformed request (`400`), which says nothing
about any organization.
Throttled and
lockout-protected — a lockout surfaces as `401 AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`,
never as a distinguishable `429`. On success the response sets the session cookie and
returns the CSRF token the client must echo on every mutation.

⚠️ **No CSRF token is required** — none can exist before a session
does, and requiring one would make first login impossible. Login is
protected instead by `Origin`/`Referer` validation against
`sm.gateway.trusted-origins`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies, and the durable
login throttle.

**Cookies set on success** (ruling `OR-21`): `__Host-SM_SESSION`
(`HttpOnly`) and `__Host-SM_CSRF` (script-readable, bound to that
session) — both `Path=/`, `SameSite=Strict`, **always** `Secure`, and
never a `Domain`, so a sibling domain cannot plant either. Plain-HTTP
deployment is not supported (`http://localhost` works in current
browsers).
The CSRF value is also returned as `csrfToken`.

⚠️ **Lockout** (rulings `OR-20`, `OR-23`, `OR-24`): a locked **client
address** is refused `401`. A locked **username** does NOT refuse a
correct credential from an unlocked address — other people's failures
can never lock the credential holder out — and a successful login clears
the username counter. Before any of this, a per-address pre-auth rate
gate answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` without doing any credential work. An operator clears a lockout with the audited
recovery command. ⛔ Behind a reverse proxy, `sm.gateway.trusted-proxies`
MUST list it, or every user would share the proxy's address — the
gateway refuses to start until the operator either lists trusted proxies
or sets `sm.gateway.direct-client-connections=true`.

⚠️ A principal whose `mustRotate` is set receives a session that
authorizes **only** `/cp/auth/identity`, `/cp/auth/logout` and
`/cp/auth/credential` until the credential is rotated. The returned
identity's `organizations` is empty in that state (ruling `OR-116`).

**Permission:** `none.establishesSession`
**Scope:** `self`

**Responses:**

- `200` — Session established.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`. ⚠️ Unknown organization, unknown user, wrong credential, inactive user and a locked-out subject return **byte-identical bodies apart from `correlationId`** — the difference must not be observable.
- `403` — `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — `Origin`/`Referer` is absent or not trusted.
- `503` — `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — retryable: a dependency did not answer. Not a credential outcome.
- `429` — `RATE_LIMITED` — the pre-authentication rate gate for this client address is exhausted. Carries `Retry-After`.

Auth: session cookie (`__Host-SM_SESSION`) from the login call plus the `X-SM-CSRF` header and a trusted `Origin` (both pre-filled).

exec: const set = (k, v) => { if (v === undefined || v === null || v === '') return; if (pm.environment.name) { pm.environment.set(k, String(v)); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, String(v)); } };
const clear = (k) => { if (pm.environment.name) { pm.environment.set(k, ''); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, ''); } };
const get = (k) => pm.variables.get(k);
pm.test('status is one this operation declares (200, 400, 401, 403, 503, 429), or 428', function () {
pm.expect([200, 400, 401, 403, 503, 429, 428]).to.include(pm.response.code);
if (pm.response.code === 428) { console.warn('MUST_ROTATE: run rotateOwnCredential in "0. Start here" first.'); }
if (pm.response.code >= 400) { try { const p = pm.response.json(); console.warn(p.code + ' correlationId=' + p.correlationId + ' ' + (p.detail || '')); } catch (e) {} }
if (pm.response.code >= 200 && pm.response.code < 300) {
let j = {}; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { j = {}; }
if (j && typeof j === 'object') {
set('csrfToken', j.csrfToken);
// Optional fallback (cookieMode=manual): keep the two Set-Cookie values for the collection pre-request script.
pm.response.headers.each(function (h) { if (h.key.toLowerCase() !== 'set-cookie') return;
const nv = String(h.value).split(';')[0];
if (nv.indexOf('__Host-SM_SESSION=') === 0) set('sessionCookie', nv);
if (nv.indexOf('__Host-SM_CSRF=') === 0) set('csrfCookie', nv); });
try { if (pm.response.json().mustRotate) console.warn('mustRotate=true: rotate the credential before anything else.'); } catch (e) {}

item.name: getIdentity · The current principal and its effective permissions

description.content:
operationId: `getIdentity`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`GET /api/cp/auth/identity`

**The current principal and its effective permissions**

⚠️ **Authentication only — no verb** (ruling `OR-15`). Requiring
`authz.introspect.self` here would make a role created without it
render an empty permission overlay for a principal who can nonetheless
act. `authz.introspect.any` still guards reading *another* principal.

organizations and sub-organizations the caller can see, by exactly the
rule `listOrganizations` / `listSubOrganizations` apply. It is empty
while `mustRotate` is true — those lists answer `428` until rotation.

**Permission:** `none.authenticationOnly`
**Scope:** `self`

**Responses:**

- `200` — The caller's identity.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.

Auth: session cookie (`__Host-SM_SESSION`) from the login call.

item.name: rotateOwnCredential · Rotate the caller's own credential

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).
Non-browser clients must send a trusted Origin on every state-changing request (login included). Must equal an entry of sm.gateway.trusted-origins.

description.content:
operationId: `rotateOwnCredential`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/cp/auth/credential`

**Rotate the caller's own credential**

⛔ **Not a catalog verb.** `LocalOperation.ROTATE_OWN_CREDENTIAL` is
cp-core-local: the catalog has 38 members and none of them is this.
Verifies the current credential, and clears `mustRotate` on success.

⚠️ **v1 scope: forced rotation only.** The operation succeeds only
while the caller's `mustRotate` is set (the bootstrap administrator,
or a principal an administrator has flagged). An ordinary self-service
password change is **not** in v1 and answers
`400 CREDENTIAL_ROTATION_REFUSED` — the same code as a wrong current
credential, deliberately, so the response does not reveal which.

**Throttled.** Wrong current credentials are counted per principal in
the durable login throttle; once locked, even a correct current
credential is refused until the lockout expires.

**Permission:** `local.rotateOwnCredential`
**Scope:** `self`

**Responses:**

- `204` — Rotated. `mustRotate` is cleared and every other session for this principal is revoked.
- `400` — `BAD_REQUEST` (malformed body, `newCredential` shorter than 12) or `CREDENTIAL_ROTATION_REFUSED` (wrong current credential, replacement equal to the current one, principal not in forced rotation, or rotation locked out) — switch on `code`.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `CSRF_REJECTED` — the token was missing or not bound to this session — or `ORIGIN_REJECTED`.
- `429` — `RATE_LIMITED` — the pre-authentication rate gate for this client address is exhausted. Carries `Retry-After`.

Auth: session cookie (`__Host-SM_SESSION`) from the login call plus the `X-SM-CSRF` header and a trusted `Origin` (both pre-filled).

exec: const set = (k, v) => { if (v === undefined || v === null || v === '') return; if (pm.environment.name) { pm.environment.set(k, String(v)); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, String(v)); } };
const clear = (k) => { if (pm.environment.name) { pm.environment.set(k, ''); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, ''); } };
const get = (k) => pm.variables.get(k);
pm.test('status is one this operation declares (204, 400, 401, 403, 429), or 428', function () {
pm.expect([204, 400, 401, 403, 429, 428]).to.include(pm.response.code);
if (pm.response.code === 428) { console.warn('MUST_ROTATE: run rotateOwnCredential in "0. Start here" first.'); }
if (pm.response.code >= 400) { try { const p = pm.response.json(); console.warn(p.code + ' correlationId=' + p.correlationId + ' ' + (p.detail || '')); } catch (e) {} }
if (pm.response.code === 204) { set('password', get('newPassword')); }  // the new credential is now the one to log in with

item.name: Setup
item.description: A fresh install, from the bootstrap credential to a registered target and a bound Operator, in the order to run it. Everything here is an ordinary request of the folders below with a body that suits the walk; each operation still has its one place in its own folder. Fill the Setup variables in the environment first (`setup*`, `ssh*`, `hostKeyFingerprint`, `allowedConfigRoot`, `allowedContainerPrefix`, `targetName`, and the secret `sshPrivateKey`), then run the folder top to bottom (or step by step: the host key is a decision, not a default). Steps are replay-safe except `rotateOwnCredential` (an already-rotated install skips it) and `createUser` (a second run answers 409 for the same username). `backend/local/sm-local.sh up` runs the same sequence through the API for the local stack; with the environment defaults this folder there replays the seeded nodes (the creates answer 200 and replay; `createUser` answers 409 for the seeded username, so `grantAssignment` needs a new username); change the `setup*` names to add new ones. A step whose request still holds a `<placeholder>` variable value stops before sending, naming the variable.

operationId: `scanHostKeys`

**Setup step 9 of 14.** Ask the host which SSH host keys it offers (writes nothing, pins nothing). The Postman console lists them; compare one with what you verified on the host and put THAT in `hostKeyFingerprint`. The scan budget is 10 a minute per session.

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/host-key-scans`

**Ask a host which SSH host keys it offers (writes nothing)**

Plan 013 T1 (D-REG 5.1 T1). The DP connects to `host:port` WITHOUT authenticating and reports the keys the
host presents, each with its algorithm. They are UNTRUSTED: nothing is pinned by this call. The user
confirms one by sending it as `hostKeyFingerprint` to `registerTarget`, which scans again and refuses a pin
the host does not offer (`HOST_KEY_NOT_OFFERED`).
`target.create` is evaluated at the body's `ownershipScope`. Rate-limited per session (default 10 a minute,
`429 RATE_LIMITED`). Recorded in the audit log (verb, scope, outcome; never the keys).
The address policy applies (`TARGET_ADDRESS_REFUSED`, OQ-3 (d)).

**Permission:** `target.create`
**Scope:** `named`

**Responses:**

- `200` — What the host offers. Never an error for a reachable host that offers keys.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `422` — `VALIDATION_FAILED` (host or port outside the grammar) or `TARGET_ADDRESS_REFUSED`.
- `429` — `RATE_LIMITED` — this session's scan budget is spent. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
- `503` — `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — the host could not be reached or presented no key.

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).

description.content:
operationId: `registerTarget`

**Setup step 10 of 14.** Register the target in both planes with its SSH key and the host key you confirmed. SM connects to the host once (a fresh scan, no authentication) before it writes anything. Plain HTTP is accepted only from a loopback peer, a TLS connection or a trusted proxy that reports `https` (`403 INSECURE_TRANSPORT` otherwise).

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/cp/targets`

**Register a deployment target with its connection record and SSH key**

Plan 013 T1.4 (D-REG 5.1 T2, 8; `BE-D54`). ONE call composes both planes, in this order: authorize
`target.create` at `ownershipScope` (writes nothing); every data-plane pre-check read-only (grammar, the key must
open as an UNENCRYPTED private key, the address policy, a fresh scan that must offer `hostKeyFingerprint`, and
no other live target of the organization holding any offered host key); then the control-plane row; then the
data-plane record with the sealed key. A refusal at any pre-check leaves NOTHING in either plane (target,
secret, event) except the scan's audit row. The pre-check's scan is a scan: it draws on the SAME per-session
budget as `scanHostKeys` (default 10 a minute, `429 RATE_LIMITED`, `Retry-After`) and is recorded in the audit
log the same way (verb, scope, outcome; never the host or the keys); a refusal before any host is contacted
(the key does not open, a field fails its grammar) is not a scan and is not recorded.
`201` new; `200` an identical replay (the same record AND the same key, compared by the fingerprint of the
key's PUBLIC half, so a re-export of one key is a replay); `409` the name is taken by a different record, the
key differs (rotate instead) or the registered key cannot be opened to compare (rotate it), a host key is held
by another live target, or the record changed under a concurrent request (retry).
⛔ `I6`: `privateKey` is write-only and is never returned, logged, audited or hashed; the only value derived
from it that any response carries is the PUBLIC key's fingerprint. `allowedConfigRoot` and
`allowedContainerPrefix` are the envelope (`B2`): immutable once registered (`OR-52`).
The request is refused `403 INSECURE_TRANSPORT`, before the body is read, unless the connection is secure, a
trusted proxy reports `https`, or the peer is loopback (OQ-14 (b)).

**Permission:** `target.create`
**Scope:** `named`

**Responses:**

- `200` — An identical replay. Nothing was written.
- `201` — Registered.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED`, `ORIGIN_REJECTED` or `INSECURE_TRANSPORT` — switch on `code`.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `CONFLICT` — the name is taken by a different record, the key is not the registered one (or the registered key cannot be opened to compare: rotate it), a host key of this machine is registered to another target, or the record changed under a concurrent request (retry).
- `422` — `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `CREDENTIAL_INVALID`, `HOST_KEY_NOT_OFFERED` or `TARGET_ADDRESS_REFUSED`.
- `429` — `RATE_LIMITED` — this session's scan budget (shared with `scanHostKeys`) is spent. Nothing was scanned or written. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
- `503` — `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — the host could not be scanned. Nothing was written; retry.

description.content:
operationId: `testTargetConnection`

**Setup step 11 of 14.** One fixed command (`docker version`) over the pinned host key and the stored key. A failure is a result, never a 5xx: read which step was not reached. Draws on the scan budget.

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/targets/{targetId}/connection/test`

**Check that a target can be reached, authenticated to, and used for Docker**

Plan 013 T1.5 (D-REG 5.1 T6; OQ-9 (a)). `target.use` at the target's own scope. Connects with the pinned host key
(the address policy first), authenticates with the stored key, and runs ONE fixed command
(`docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'`; no input reaches it). An unreachable host, a host that presents
another key than the pin, a key the host refuses, a stopped Docker daemon and a user outside the `docker` group are
each a RESULT with the steps not reached set `false`, never a `5xx`. Writes nothing; recorded in the audit log
(verb `target.use`, the target, the furthest step reached; never the host, the version or any message).
`404` when the target has no live connection record.

It is a probe, so it is bounded like one (review W4C-4): it draws on the SAME per-session budget as `scanHostKeys`,
`registerTarget` and `editTargetConnection` (default 10 a minute), and only one test of a target runs at a time.
Either refusal is `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`, makes no connection, and is recorded as a `DENY` row of
`target.use` with the reason `rate_limited`. Whether tests should have a budget of their own is an open owner
question (W3C-2, W4C-4).

**Agent targets** (plan 015 T3.5): a target whose `transport` is `agent` has no address to connect to; this answers `409 TARGET_TRANSPORT_UNSUPPORTED`, no SSH connection is made, and the per-session probe budget is not drawn.

**Scope:** `named`

- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `TARGET_TRANSPORT_UNSUPPORTED` — the target's transport is `agent`: there is no SSH connection to test. No connection was made and no budget was drawn.

`target.create` at `ownershipScope` (writes nothing); every data-plane pre-check read-only (grammar, the key must

**Issue a one-time enrolment token for a host agent (shown once)**

Plan 015 T4.3 (`OR-126` A8, `OR-128` (4)). Requires `agent.enrol` **and** `target.create` at the environment: enrolment
creates the agent's target (`BE-D71`), so the issuer must hold the right to create one. The environment is the path's;
no organization or environment appears in the body (`I5`).

The response carries the token **once** (`readOnly`): it is never returned by `getAgent` or `listAgents`, never logged,
never audited and stored only as an unkeyed SHA-256 digest of 256 random bits (`OR-128` (9)). `targetName` is checked
here against the organization's live target names and against the names pending tokens hold, and a taken one is
`409 CONFLICT` (nothing written); the unique index on the target row remains the backstop at enrolment. The envelope
(`allowedConfigRoot`, `allowedContainerPrefix`) is fixed by this call and immutable: it becomes the agent target's envelope
and bounds every placement `OR-27` registers. A structurally malformed body (unparseable, a required field missing, a stray
property) is `400`; an envelope value that fails its rule (`allowedConfigRoot`, `allowedContainerPrefix`) is `422`, as it is
for `registerTarget`.

unless set, bounded by `token-max-validity`, 30 days unless set; `OR-136` (1)); `expiresAt` says when. The agent's
**capabilities are fixed by the server** (`apply-config`, `lifecycle`) and are not a body field: an agent issued none would
refuse every command. `report-only` is not issued (central item `AGW-12` is routed).

agent's auto-registered instances are. The entitlement and the instance quota are enforced when those instances register
(`OR-27`, `OR-40`), not here. The call writes `agent_registration` under the audit operation `AGENT_ENROLMENT_ISSUED`
with the issuing principal as actor.

reports `https`, or the peer is loopback: the response carries a credential (`OQ-14 (b)`).

`POST /api/cp/agents/{agentId}/revoke`

**Revoke an agent (sticky)**

operationId: `declareInstance`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/environments/{environmentId}/instances`

**Declare an instance**

Requires `instance.create` at the environment **and** `instance.bindTarget`
plus `target.use` for the target being bound — `D10`'s two-sided rule.

⚠️ **Path moved to the environment** (owner ruling 2026-09-29 (S0-8), `OR-52`):
`instance.create` is checked at the environment (`OR-27`) and the resource is resolved
**before the body is read** (`ResourceResolver.java` javadoc), so the environment cannot
come from the body.

**The body names a host path and a container only inside the target's own envelope**
(Global Constraints, B2) — `containerName` inside `allowedContainerPrefix` and
`configDirectory` inside `allowedConfigRoot`, both fixed at target registration (T2.7).
Anything else is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the field, never echoing the value —
enforced by the service, a database trigger, and the adapter's canonical-path preflight.

**`acquisition` is the per-instance acquisition mode** (owner rulings M-Q2 and M-Q2b,
2026-09-29; the address question ruled by `OR-82`, 2026-10-05): the operator **chooses**
the mode here — `direct-http` (the DP polls the **target's registered address**, fixed
when an operator registered the target (T2.7), at the placement's `healthPort` and the
package-declared health path, over HTTP; offered first) or `via-ssh` (the DP curls the
host's loopback over the target's SSH session) — and the DP persists the **mode** at
**instance** level, so it survives a re-target's new placement. **The body carries no
host and no address of any kind** (`OR-82`): nothing about where the DP connects comes
from the browser, so an `instance.create` holder cannot point the DP at an arbitrary
address, and a re-target polls the new target's own address with no carried-forward value.
**No automatic fallback**: a failing path reads `unreachable`, it never switches. One
setting governs both health polling (M-Q2b, amending `OR-39`) and metrics collection.
Changing it later is a future operation, not part of v1.

`healthPort` is the host-side port the engine reaches over the chosen mode (M12). The
probe's `kind`, `path` and `strength` come from the package's **declared** `health.probe`
(`contracts/solution-package.schema.json`, `T0.1a`), resolved by the gateway at declare —
never from this body.

**The host binding: exactly one of `targetId` and `connectionId`** (integration plan 014).
New declarations select `deploymentMode: dp-remote` (the default when absent) and bind a
**remote-server Connection** by `connectionId`; `targetId` remains for older clients and
existing instances. Neither is in `required`, because "exactly one of" cannot be said beside
`additionalProperties: false` without restructuring the body into a `oneOf`: a body naming
**both or neither** is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `connectionId`. A `connectionId` that is
not an **active `remote-server`** Connection of the organization, or whose data-plane runtime
projection is not live, is `422` naming `connectionId` (fail closed: no fallback to a Target,
and the browser never supplies a host). `host-local` and `federated` are reserved and refused
`422` naming `deploymentMode`. For a connection-backed declare, `instance.bindTarget` is asked
at the environment and `target.use` at the **Connection's** ownership scope (plan 014: the
same checks, mapped to the Connection resource). ⚠️ A connection-backed placement records no
metrics endpoints and is neither applied, probed nor collected until plan 014 step 3 resolves
the host through the Connection: until then it fails closed (`unreachable`, target unavailable).
**Agent targets** (plan 015 T3.5): a declare that names an agent target answers `409 TARGET_IS_AGENT_MANAGED`: an agent's instances register themselves from discovery (`OR-27`). Nothing was written.

**Scope:** `environment`

- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.

- `422` — `VALIDATION_FAILED` — names the field. Never echoes the value. An `acquisition` carrying any property other than `mode` (a host, in particular — `OR-82`) is refused.

description.content:
operationId: `addPlacement`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/placements`

**Add a placement to an instance**

Gives an **active** instance another placement — a second container on another target (or a second one on the same
target, with its own container name, config directory and ports) — in one data-plane transaction that locks the
instance row and re-checks `active` (`BE-D47`). Writes **no host and deploys nothing**: the customer's CI/CD deploys
the container and the operator names it here (`OR-29`, `I1`).

Requires `instance.bindTarget` **at the instance** (`OR-16`; ruled in `OR-121`, OQ-8.3s (i)) **and** `target.use` at
the target named in the body — `D10`'s two-sided rule. A binding scoped to one instance can add placements to that
instance only. Does **not** count against the organization's instance quota: a placement is not an instance
(`OR-121`, OQ-8.8 (a)).

**The body is `declareInstance`'s `placement` object plus the `targetId`**, with the same envelope: `containerName`
inside the target's `allowedContainerPrefix` and `configDirectory` inside its `allowedConfigRoot` (`B2`; anything
else is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the field, never the value). **The probe's `kind`, `path` and `strength` and
the metrics definitions come from the instance's DECLARED package version — never from this body.** `healthPort` and
`metricsPorts` are host-side ports on the **new** target, as at declare; the body carries no host or address
(`OR-82`) and `acquisition` is the instance's own, not repeated here.

⚠️ **What the new placement starts as** (`OR-121`, OQ-8.10 (a)): unconverged, and said so. Until a fleet rolls the
instance's current generation to it, the configuration ladder reads `rendered` (the lowest rung across live
placements), `instance.config-state` is announced if the stored rung moved, `getHealth` reports it unpolled and then
— if the container is not deployed yet — `unreachable`, which is true. **Next:** roll the current generation to the
new placement with `submitFleetApply` (one member) or `submitApply`.

⚠️ **A package that declares push metrics (`solace_event` sources) is refused `409`** (OQ-8.9 (a)): a push reading
is attributed to a placement by the instance key in its payload, which names no placement and, with two, would be
dropped as ambiguous — and `I1` forbids a placement field in the MI's event. Pull-path metrics are per placement and
unaffected. Only an `active` instance takes a placement: a pending, abandoned, unknown or another organization's
instance is the same `404`.

⚠️ **Refused `409` while an instance-wide request is in flight** (`REQUESTED`, `RUNNING` or `APPLY_INDETERMINATE`;
in practice an instance-wide stop): an instance-wide stop reads the live placements **once, when it starts running**,
so a placement added under it would be left running by a stop that then reports the instance stopped. The check is
made holding the instance's admission lock, as `retirePlacement`'s is. Add after it lands.

⚠️ **The add stamps the instance** (it changes what the instance reads as), so a designer session that staged
against the earlier `stateVersion` is refused `409` (a stale `baseStateVersion`) on its next `stageConfig` and must re-read.

The acting principal is recorded on the placement row as `created_by` (`OR-125` (1), `sm_data` V026). A placement
that pre-dates V026 has no recorded actor.

**Agent targets** (plan 015 T3.5): placements on an agent target come only from `OR-27` discovery in v1; naming one answers `409 TARGET_IS_AGENT_MANAGED` and writes nothing.

**Permission:** `instance.bindTarget` + also `target.use`
**Scope:** `instance`

**Responses:**

- `201` — Added. The instance as it reads now: every live placement, and a fresh `stateVersion` (the add stamped the instance).
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `CONFLICT` — a placement collision (`OR-29`: this target already has a live placement with that container name, config directory or health port), the instance's package declares push metrics (`OR-121`, OQ-8.9 (a)) or an instance-wide request is in flight on the instance (a stop reads the live set o…
- `422` — `VALIDATION_FAILED` — names the field (`targetId` not a live target of this organization, or a `placement` field outside the target's envelope or its grammar). Never echoes the value.

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).
Non-browser clients must send a trusted Origin on every state-changing request (login included). Must equal an entry of sm.gateway.trusted-origins.

query.description: Must be `leave-running`; retiring a placement never stops or removes its container.

variable.description: A placement of the instance named in the same path (`OR-2`); never a grant level (`OR-16`).

description.content:
operationId: `retirePlacement`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`DELETE /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/placements/{placementId}`

**Retire one placement of an instance**

Retires **one** live placement (`BE-D53`; ruled in `OR-121`, plan 012 `OPS-Q12` R-1): the row is kept forever, marked
retired, and its container name, config directory and ports become free for `addPlacement` again.

⛔ **It never touches the host.** The container keeps running — now **unmanaged by SM** — and the response says so
(`workload: left-running`). The request must say so too: `?workload=leave-running` is **required**, and any other
value or none is `400`, so a caller who expected the container to be removed is told before anything happens.

Requires `instance.bindTarget` at the instance — the verb that adds a placement also removes one; `target.use` is not
asked, because removal touches no target.

**Refused `409`** for the instance's **last** live placement (that is releasing the instance from management,
undeclare) and while work is in flight that names it: a `REQUESTED`, `RUNNING` or `APPLY_INDETERMINATE` request on it
**or on the whole instance** (an instance-wide stop addresses every live placement), or a fleet that still reserves it,
**or a `PENDING` scheduled apply that names the placement** (a distinct `409` detail that names no schedule: cancel the
placement's pending schedules, then retire it; Fable F-3, `OR-131` Q2 by analogy).
The in-flight check is made holding the instance's admission lock, so no request can be admitted between the check and
the retirement. An instance-wide stop issued afterwards addresses only the **remaining** live placements (`BE-D46`).

⚠️ **A window this does not close** (W2 review W2A-3): a `submitApply` or a `submitFleetApply` validates that its
placement is live **before** admission, and admission does not re-check it. One that validated the placement a moment
before it was retired is then admitted for a retired placement, and **fails visibly** at its preflight (a failed
request, or a fleet that ends `COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES` or halts) rather than being refused up front. Nothing is
applied to the host. Retire a placement when nothing of yours is being submitted for it.

⚠️ **The retirement stamps the instance**, so a designer session that staged against the earlier `stateVersion`
is refused `409` (a stale `baseStateVersion`) on its next `stageConfig` and must re-read.

The acting principal is recorded on the placement row as `retired_by`, with `retired_at` (`OR-125` (1), `sm_data`
V026).
Plan 012 T5 (`OPS-Q12` R-1) also writes, in the same data-plane transaction, a placement-scoped `instance_retirement`
row — the session principal, the request's correlation id, the disposition `leave-running` and the placement's last
persisted health state — already closed `retired`. A refused retirement writes neither record.

Afterwards the configuration ladder is re-settled: retiring the placement that lagged raises the instance's rung, and
`instance.config-state` is announced if the stored rung moved.

**Permission:** `instance.bindTarget`
**Scope:** `instance`

**Responses:**

- `200` — Retired. The workload was left running, and the instance reads without the placement.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.

- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `CONFLICT` — the placement is the instance's last live placement, or work is in flight that names it. Switch on the problem's `detail`; neither names the request, the fleet nor another instance.

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).

description.content:
operationId: `undeclareInstance`

⚠️ **Run this one LAST. It releases the instance `{{instanceId}}` from management; every request that uses that instance afterwards answers `404`. Declare a fresh instance (`declareInstance`) to try it without losing the one the rest of the collection uses. The container on the host is never touched.**

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`DELETE /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}`

**Undeclare an instance**

Releases the instance from SM's inventory and management (`BE-D49`; ruled in `OR-121`, `OPS-Q2` **U-C**): afterwards it
is not listed or readable, SM polls nothing on it, collects no metrics from it, admits no apply to it, and it no longer
counts against the organization's quota (`OR-40`). **Nothing is deleted** — every row moves to a terminal state and
stays — and ids are never reused.

⛔ **It never touches the host.** The container keeps running — now **unmanaged by SM** — together with its config file
and the `.sm-preimage-*` and `.sm-fp-*` files SM wrote beside it (the file holds the secrets the container uses; the
pre-images may hold older ones). Cleaning them is the operator's, and `docs/runbooks/operations.md` gives the exact
commands. The request must say so: `?workload=leave-running` is **required**, and any other value or none is `400`,
so a caller who expected the container to be stopped or removed is told before anything happens. To stop it first, call
`stopInstance` (`instance.stop`) and wait for it to land.

Requires `instance.undeclare` at the instance (`HIGH`; Administrator and Operator). Authorization is at the owning
instance (`OR-16`); placements are not a grant level.

**Refused `409`** while anything is in flight on the instance: a `REQUESTED` or `RUNNING` apply or stop, an
unresolved `APPLY_INDETERMINATE` request (there is no API to resolve one by hand — `OPS-Q5`, a known gap), or a
`RUNNING` fleet that still reserves one of its placements, **or while a `PENDING` apply schedule names the instance**
(`OR-131`): cancel the instance's pending schedules first (`cancelApplySchedule`), then undeclare. The check is made
holding the instance's admission lock, which `submitApply` and `rollbackApply` (with a `schedule`) also take before it inserts, so an undeclare and an
admission, or an undeclare and a schedule created at the same moment, cannot both win. `detail` names which kind, never
another request's id.

**Two planes, three steps** (`ops-501.md` §4.4): the data plane records the intent and takes the instance out of every
read (`retiring`), the control plane releases the governance node (audited `INSTANCE_UNDECLARED`, naming the
requesting session), and the data plane finishes (`retired`; its placements retired). A crash between the steps is
finished by **retrying this call** (an authorized retry resumes and answers `200`; the control-plane audit row names
the retrying principal, the data-plane record keeps the original requester) or by a lazy sweep that runs inside
`declareInstance`, `listInstances` and `getInstance` for the requesting organization only: it completes an undeclare
whose control-plane step is done, and **rolls back** one that is not once `sm.dp.undeclare.rollback-after` (default
ten minutes) has passed — the instance then simply reappears. A request that finds its own record older than **half**
that window answers `503` and the control plane is not written, so a roll-back can never race a slow control-plane step.
Retry once the whole window has passed: a retry that finds its own record older than the **whole** window runs the same
sweep for the requesting organization (rolling the stale record back), then begins again on the clean record and
proceeds; it does not wait for another request to run the sweep. Between half the window and the whole window every
retry is `503` by design.

**A repeated call is `404`**, as for an unknown id: a retired instance, one whose control-plane node is already
released, and one that never was this organization's are indistinguishable.

⚠️ **Residues, accepted** (`OPS-Q4` (a)): the instance's role bindings stay but grant and reveal nothing; metric history
stays until partition retention and is unreachable through the API; an `APPLY_INDETERMINATE` request blocks undeclare
until the reconciler resolves it.

**Permission:** `instance.undeclare`
**Scope:** `instance`

**Responses:**

- `200` — Undeclared. The workload was left running; each placement is listed with the last health state SM had persisted.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `CONFLICT` — something is in flight on the instance (a request, a fleet reservation or a `PENDING` apply schedule). Switch on the problem's `detail`; it names the kind, never the request, the fleet or another instance.
- `503` — `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — this request's own data-plane record is older than half the roll-back window, so the control plane was **not** written; retry. The instance may read as released and reappear once the window passes.

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).

description.content:
operationId: `acceptRuntimeConfig`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/config/accept-runtime`

**Accept observed runtime drift as the new intended configuration**

Contracted by ruling `OR-45` (console-integration.md §5.2 row 42); served by plan 010 T10.4 as ruled by
`OR-104` (`D-ACCEPT`, [`accept-runtime.md`](../../docs/design/backend/accept-runtime.md)).
Accepting drift is an OVERRIDE, not a plain edit — both `config.edit` and
`config.overrideWarning` are required. **Writes nothing to the host.**

It reads the named placement's own config file back (one bounded read; the request names no path,
host or command) and stages what it can map as a new generation with `origin accept-runtime`,
through the same server-side half `stageConfig` runs (`OR-34`): the server re-projects, refuses an
undeclared key or a blocking validation, and stores its own result.

- **Keys the package does not declare** are accepted-around, not refused: they are listed by
  **path only** in `notAccepted[]` (capped at 200, `truncated`), and ⚠️ **the next apply removes
  them from the host**, because the file is rebuilt from the generation. SM's own overlay keys are
  listed `sm-owned-overlay`; a host edit of one is not adopted. Only the exact declared kebab
  path is mapped: any other spelling (`maxSize`, `max_size`) is listed `undeclared-key`.
- ⛔ **`I6`: a secret field's value is never stored.** The draft keeps its current `secretRef`. The
  field is listed `secret-not-read`, and `comparison` says `same` or `differs`: the data plane
  compared the file's value with the stored secret in memory and reports only that. ⚠️ A `differs`
  secret **is reverted by the next apply** (the generation still points at the stored one). The
  value never reaches the gateway, a response, a log or an event.
- A `yaml`-typed field is never accepted (`yaml-field-not-accepted`); it keeps what it holds.
- `fileBytesDifferFromRendered` is true when the file read back is not byte-identical to SM's
  rendering of the returned `generation`: the file is not rewritten until that generation is
  applied (a `manual` apply rewrites it in SM's canonical form, with no restart).
- `unchanged` (OR-33 guard 1) with a non-empty `notAccepted` is a legitimate answer.

**`placementId` added and required** (ratified, Step 7 sitting 2026-09-30, batch 1,
point 18): which placement's file is read back. The config of record is per instance, so
accepting one placement's file changes the instance's desired configuration for every placement.

**One placement, one instance generation** (`BE-D45`): this operation names one placement but
mints a new **instance** generation, because configuration is per instance. The instance's other
placements are not changed and read as behind: the config ladder reports the lowest rung across
the instance's live placements, so the instance reads as not converged until a fleet applies the
new generation to them (`submitFleetApply`, one member per placement).

enough.

with no health gate, so each **also** needs `instance.restart.overrideSafety` (`OPS-Q6` B-1,

outage and needs `outageConfirmedBy` (`400` without it); the server records the **session
principal's id**, not the string sent (`OPS-Q7` C-2). **Refusal order** (the interceptor checks
the primary verb before the body is read): `404`/`403` (`config.apply`) → `400` (body, including the missing
`restart-all` confirmation, and a malformed `schedule`) → `422` (`strategy: scheduled`, see below) → `403`

is not live) → the data plane's refusals (`409`/`422`). On a single placement the two behave as follows
(`BE-D23`): both restart the one container and verify the read-back — they differ from
`rolling-health-gated` only in having no gate, and from each other only in the confirmation.

name): add `schedule: {notBefore, notAfter}` and the change is **recorded, not admitted** — the response is `202`

ordinary apply is admitted with the **submitter** as its actor — a submitter who has since lost a verb or been

whose window closed first is `MISSED`. `notBefore` must be in the future and at most

operationId: `rollbackApply`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/apply/rollback`

**Roll back to a prior generation**

**Operator rollback copies forward** (ruling `OR-42`, ⚠️ names `B/D12` 🔒 — for
architect-group ratification): a new generation takes the CHOSEN PRIOR
generation's content, then a normal apply runs it with `BE-D22`'s pre-image
safety net. Rollback never rewinds the generation counter — the only-goes-up
fence stays, and this rule is the same for `dp-remote` and the agent.

**The target is named one of two ways** — exactly one of `applyId` or `generation` must be
given, and they are NOT equivalent:
- `applyId`: **undo that apply**. The target is the highest eligible generation BELOW
  that apply's generation on this `placementId` (`409` if none). `applyId` must be an apply
  of this `placementId`; one of another placement, or of another instance, is `404`.
- `generation`: copy that generation forward directly (when no `applyId` is at hand).

⚠️ **Eligibility:** the named target must be a generation ACTUALLY WRITTEN to
this `placementId` — `STAGED`, `APPLIED`, or `SUPERSEDED` after having been staged, or an
apply an operator resolved `INDETERMINATE_RESOLVED` with outcome `applied` (confirmed on
the host; ruling `OR-108` (7), extending `OR-42`'s list). Resolved as `not_applied` is not
a target. A generation the engine never wrote to this placement is not a rollback target and
is refused `409`.

**`placementId` is required** (ratified, Step 7 sitting 2026-09-30, batch 1, point 12): a
rollback is an apply, and v1 refuses instance-wide apply (`BE-D23`) — an absent
`placementId` would always answer an error, so the landed (`9ec6797`) optional/nullable
shape is replaced to match `submitApply` (point 10).

**One placement, one instance generation** (`BE-D45`): this operation names one placement but
mints a new **instance** generation, because configuration is per instance. The instance's other
placements are not changed and read as behind: the config ladder reports the lowest rung across
the instance's live placements, so the instance reads as not converged until a fleet applies the
new generation to them (`submitFleetApply`, one member per placement).

**`rolling-no-validation` and `restart-all`** (plan 012 T2, `OR-121`) are served: each also needs
`instance.restart.overrideSafety` (`OPS-Q6` B-1), and `restart-all` needs `outageConfirmedBy`
(`OPS-Q7` C-2; the server records the session principal). **A refused rollback mints no
generation:** the `400` (missing confirmation) and the `403` (a verb) are answered **before**
the copy-forward, so a refused `restart-all` rollback leaves the instance's generation count
unchanged. **Refusal order** (the interceptor checks the primary verb before the body is read):
`404`/`403` (`config.rollback`) → `400` (body, including the missing `restart-all` confirmation and a malformed
`schedule`) → `422` (`strategy: scheduled`) → `403` (`instance.restart`, then `instance.restart.overrideSafety`) →
`404` (the instance is not active, or the placement is not live) → the data plane's refusals (`409`/`422`).

**Scheduling** (plan 012 T7, `OPS-Q9` Sch-2): add `schedule: {notBefore, notAfter}` as for `submitApply` and the
rollback is **recorded, not run** — `202` with a `scheduleId` and no `applyId`. ⚠️ **The copy-forward happens when the
window opens, not at submit**: a copy at 14:00 would make old content the instance's desired head twelve hours
early. At fire the target is resolved again (a generation that stopped being eligible closes the schedule
`REFUSED`, `schedule.rollback.target-not-eligible`), and the new generation is minted **above whatever was staged
meanwhile**; the schedule then records the target it resolved and the number it minted. The submitter is asked for
`config.rollback` (and `instance.restart` / `instance.restart.overrideSafety` as the `strategy` needs) now **and
again at fire**. A scheduled rollback of a generation that is, by then, behind a newer applied one is refused by the
monotonicity fence as any apply is (`schedule.generation.superseded`).

**Agent placements** (plan 015 T3.3): a placement whose target's transport is `agent` answers `501 AGENT_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` at admission (the rollback's `restore` step is not available to an agent), so no doomed apply request is admitted and no generation is minted.

**Permission:** `config.rollback` + also `instance.restart`, `instance.restart.overrideSafety`
**Scope:** `instance`

- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `501` — `AGENT_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` — the placement's target is an agent: this operation is not available on it in v1. Nothing was read or written and no SSH connection was made.
- `409` — Not an eligible rollback target for this placement (never written, or not `STAGED`/`APPLIED`/`SUPERSEDED`-after-staging/resolved-as-applied), or another apply or a stop is already in flight for this scope (refused before anything is copied). ⚠️ A refusal AFTER the copy (a race with another admissio…

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).
Non-browser clients must send a trusted Origin on every state-changing request (login included). Must equal an entry of sm.gateway.trusted-origins.

description.content:
operationId: `stopInstance`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/stop`

**Stop an instance, or one of its placements**

⛔ **HIGH consequence, audited, idempotent** — catalog row 36,
assigned to plan 007 Task 6b by ruling `OR-18`. Held by the
**Administrator and the Operator**: `OR-121` (`OPS-Q11` (a), written as
`D10` §1.9) gave the Operator `instance.stop`; it was Administrator-only
before that.

**Targeting, exactly as the engine executes it** (`BE-D26`): one
placement, or the whole instance. **An absent `placementId` means
instance-wide** and is sent to the engine as the nil-UUID sentinel
`PlacementId.INSTANCE_WIDE`; an instance-wide stop addresses every
placement of the instance and lands under **one** `applyId`. Two
placements whose containers share a name are both stopped (`BE-D44`:
the apply journal records each intent under its own placement).

⚠️ **Which placements** (`BE-D46`): the stop addresses every **live**
placement, read from the placement registry and never from request
history. A retired placement (`retirePlacement`) is not addressed, so
retiring one never fails a later instance-wide stop, and a placement
added by `addPlacement` is addressed by every instance-wide stop that
**starts running after** it exists. A stop reads the live set once, when
it starts running, so `addPlacement` is refused `409` while an
instance-wide request is in flight, rather than being missed by it.

⚠️ **Authorized at the OWNING INSTANCE scope** (ruling `OR-16`).
Placement is an operational child identity, not a grantable level, so
a binding cannot grant `stop` for one placement only.

⛔ **No `generation`, no `strategy`, no `outageConfirmedBy`.** The
engine's `ApplyCommand` rejects all three on a stop; accepting them
would be an API that cannot execute.

**Idempotent:** stopping an already-stopped instance returns `202` and
still writes one audit line. ⚠️ Failures land *after* admission and
therefore still return `202`, surfacing as a terminal `STOP_FAILED` on
the request: `stop.no.known.placement` (instance-wide against an
instance with no live placement) and a replica that could not be
stopped. There is no label-collision failure: two placements that
share a replica label are journalled separately and both stopped.

**Permission:** `instance.stop`
**Scope:** `instance`

**Responses:**

- `202` — Stop admitted and durable. ⚠️ Does not mean the workload stopped — observe the request for its terminal state.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.

item.name: submitFleetApply · Submit one apply across several instances

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).

description.content:
operationId: `submitFleetApply`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/fleet-applies`

**Submit one apply across several instances**

`x-sm-scope: reach` (`OR-57`): the pre-handler check is `config.apply` held at ≥ 1 grant
anywhere in the caller's organization (else `403`); the handler then `require`s each
member at its own instance (fleet-apply.md §2.3) — still one enforcement point, as
declare's secondary verbs are. `instance.restart` is required in addition, in the
handler, only when `strategy` restarts anything — and **`instance.restart.overrideSafety`**
as well for `rolling-no-validation` and `restart-all` (plan 012 T2, `OR-121`, `OPS-Q6` B-1):
a member refused on any of them is `FORBIDDEN` in `refusedMembers[]`, exactly as for
`instance.restart` (`OR-65` Q-F5), so a fleet whose caller holds the verb at one instance
and not another admits one member and refuses the other, and is `403` when every member is
refused. `restart-all` needs `outageConfirmedBy` (`400` without it); the server records the
**session principal's id** on the fleet and on each member's request (`OPS-Q7` C-2).

**Refusal order:** the reach pre-check (`403`) → `400` (body, including the missing `restart-all`
confirmation) → `422` (`scheduled`: a fleet cannot be scheduled) → the per-member verdicts (`config.apply`, `instance.restart`,
`instance.restart.overrideSafety`, each at the member's own instance) → `403` for a fleet with refused
members unless `proceedWithAuthorized` → the data plane's `422`s (the per-member checks, then the
repeated-instance rule, `fleet.batch.instance.repeated`) → `409` (a placement is already reserved).

**Fleet safety across one instance's placements** (`OPS-Q8`, `BE-D50`; plan 012 T6): batches are made of
`members[]` in order — member `k` is in batch `k / batchSize`. For the **rolling** strategies
(`rolling-health-gated`, `rolling-no-validation`) a batch may hold **at most one placement of any
instance**: a batch that holds two is refused whole at submit with `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` and the
detail `member N shares its batch with another placement of its instance (fleet.batch.instance.repeated)`
— `N` is the member that repeats an instance already in its batch (the first such member, so for
`[a, a, a]` in one batch `N` is `1`), and nothing is written. A member the caller was
refused (`refusedMembers[]`) never counts. `restart-all` is exempt (its `outageConfirmedBy` covers the
multi-placement outage, up to `batchSize` placements of an instance at once) and so is `manual`, which
restarts nothing. Separately, a **`rolling-no-validation`** fleet waits between batches: the next batch
opens no earlier than the data plane's settle delay (`sm.dp.fleet.no-validation.settle`, default 30 s,
`0` disables it) after the **last** member of the current batch reached its terminal time, measured from
the persisted request timestamps and so unchanged by a restart of the data plane. For a member whose
request ended `APPLY_INDETERMINATE` and was given up on by the reconciler, which has no terminal time, the
instant is the moment the reconciler gave up (its persisted `gave_up_at`), so that member holds the wait
too (`BE-D50` rider, 2026-10-08, W4B-1). The delay is the same
between every pair of batches, and the last batch lands the fleet without waiting. `rolling-health-gated` waits on its own gate, and `restart-all` and `manual` do not
wait. So the safe shape for a rolling restart of an instance's placements is `batchSize: 1` (one at a
time, at least the settle delay apart), or one placement of each instance per batch.

**Scope of these rules: one fleet.** The repeated-instance rule and the settle delay apply **within one
fleet** only. A placement is reserved, and an apply scope is held, per placement, so another fleet, or a
single-placement apply (`submitApply`, `rollbackApply`, `restoreRuntimeConfig`), may restart a **different**
placement of the same instance while this fleet runs; it is neither refused nor delayed by this fleet. Each
action still needs its own authorization. Protection per instance across actions would be a new ruling (an
instance-level reservation), not part of these rules.

**By default the whole action is refused**, listing the refused members — nothing is
applied. `proceedWithAuthorized: true` instead admits the authorized members and reports
the rest (`OR-57`). Never a silent partial action.

Each member is staged (`OR-34` re-projection) **before** the fleet is submitted — a
fleet never copies forward inside the submit transaction (Global Constraints: lock
order).

**Rolling a generation across an instance's placements** (`BE-D45`): an apply names one
placement, and there is no instance-wide apply. Two placements of one instance are two
members of a fleet — `(instanceId, placementA)` and `(instanceId, placementB)` — each its own
placement-scoped request with its own journal, batched by `batchSize` and `onFailure`
(`halt-remaining` stops after the first failed batch). Configuration is per instance, so every
placement receives the same generation; to give different placements different content,
submit a `manual` fleet per placement (each member's generation is its own staged content,
and SM does not check that members' generations are "the same change").

operationId: `exportLogs`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`GET /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/logs/{component}/export`

**Download the collected log of one agent placement**

Streams the log the host-local agent collected for one placement as a plain-text download
(`Content-Disposition: attachment`), oldest first, one line per log line: an RFC 3339 instant, a space, the line's text.
**Agent placements only**: a placement on an SSH target answers `501 AGENT_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` and nothing is read
(there is no SSH export).

⚠️ **SM does not redact log lines.** A line is the managed integration's own output (a stack trace can carry a
connection string); `logs.read` is the only control, so grant it narrowly. It is the same verb as `readLogs`.

**Bounded.** The download stops at the data plane's `sm.dp.logs.export-max-bytes` (the size of the **download**: every
UTF-8 byte written counts, markers included; default 50 MiB, minimum 1024) or `sm.dp.logs.export-deadline` (default 5
minutes). At most `sm.dp.logs.export-max-concurrent` exports run at once on the data plane and
`sm.gateway.logs.export-max-threads` on the gateway, which has its own threads, separate from the metrics export's. The
stream is pulled as the client reads it, so a slow client slows the agent; a client that disconnects cancels the agent's
request.

**Refused before the first byte, as a status.** `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `reason: log-export-concurrency` (too many exports
running, `Retry-After`), `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with a fixed `detail` when the agent cannot serve it now (not connected, no
log support, not collecting, busy, silent, or its connection ended) - the data plane waits up to
`sm.dp.logs.export-start-timeout` (default 5s) for the agent's first answer so these are known before the response starts -
`404` for an unknown or foreign instance, component or placement, `400` for an ambiguous placement and `501` for an SSH
placement.

**Marker lines** are for what happens after the first byte. Each starts with `# sm-export:` and its text is fixed by SM (it
never names a host, path, container or secret): `gap <REASON> from <instant> to <instant>` where the collected log has a hole
(`REASON` is one of `DROPPED_OLDEST`, `COLLECTION_PAUSED`, `CONTAINER_UNREADABLE`, `CAP_REDUCED`, `OVERSIZE`, or `UNKNOWN`);
`truncated: the size limit was reached`, `truncated: the time limit was reached`, `incomplete: the agent's connection was
lost`, `incomplete: the agent could not read the rest of the log` (the agent hit a read error and ended the export early) and
`incomplete: the export ended unexpectedly`, each followed by `; resume from seq <n>`; and `complete, with gaps` as the last
line of a finished download that had gaps. **A download that ends cleanly with no marker, or with `complete, with gaps`, is
complete; every `truncated` and `incomplete` marker means it is not.** After the first byte, an error in the stream or the gateway's backstop timeout writes the `incomplete` marker where the response is still writable and
then **aborts the connection without the chunked terminator**, so the client sees a failed transfer; it never appends an error body (a shutdown interrupt writes the same marker and ends the body normally). A line longer
than half the size budget is cut and ends with `[line truncated]`, and so does a line the agent itself cut. To resume, call again
with `fromSeq=<n>`; that may repeat up to one chunk of lines already written, never lose any. An export that loses its agent sends no final chunk, so it ends at
the deadline with a marker rather than hanging.

Once the first byte is sent the status cannot change, which is why everything after that point is a marker line, not an HTTP error.

**Scope:** `instance`

- `429` — `RATE_LIMITED`, `reason: log-export-concurrency` - too many log exports are running (the data plane's cap or the gateway's own threads). Nothing was sent. Carries `Retry-After`.
- `503` — `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` - the agent cannot serve the export now; `detail` is a fixed reason that names no host or container. Nothing was sent.
- `501` — `AGENT_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` — the placement is on an SSH target: only agent placements can be exported. Nothing was read and no SSH connection was made.

item.name: setLogLevel · Change the log level

header.description: Session-bound CSRF token (login/identity response).
Non-browser clients must send a trusted Origin on every state-changing request (login included). Must equal an entry of sm.gateway.trusted-origins.

description.content:
operationId: `setLogLevel`

**SERVED — implemented by the production launcher today.**

`POST /api/dp/instances/{instanceId}/log-levels/{component}`

**Change the log level**

High-consequence and audited. **Ruled (`OR-103`, option Rd): every level change is
configuration, and there is no live write in v1.** `mode: config` stages a new configuration
generation whose SM-owned overlay sets `logging.level.<logger>` for the package-declared
logger (never a request field), and admits an ordinary apply of it (`manual`: the file is
written and nothing restarts), answering `202 ApplyAccepted`; observe it at `/apply/observe`.
The level takes effect **when the service next restarts**; `getLogLevel` reports it as
`configuredLevel` beside the running `liveLevel`. The same scope fence as any apply holds:
`409 CONFLICT` while another apply or restart holds the placement. ⚠️ **A `409` that loses a race leaves
the change staged** (W2-12): the scope is checked before anything is minted, but an apply admitted in the
instant between that check and this request's own admission is refused after the new generation was
committed. That generation is then the instance's latest, so `getLogLevel` reports its `configuredLevel`
and the next apply of the instance writes it. Re-submit the change (it is answered as unchanged and
admits the staged generation) once the other apply has finished. A designer edit staged and not yet
applied is never carried by a level change: it is refused `409 CONFLICT` (`UNAPPLIED_DRAFT_PENDING`, W2-01),
and needs its own `config.apply`. A package that declares no
`logs.loggers` has nothing to change: `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`. `mode: live` answers
`501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (the live write is a documented later step, not built), except on a
direct-HTTP-only placement, where it answers `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` (`OR-43`: configuration
only). `OR-103` decided against a journaled live-set operation, so there is no fourth
`ApplyObservation.operation` member and no `V013` for it.

**One placement, one instance generation** (`BE-D45`): this operation names one placement but
mints a new **instance** generation, because configuration is per instance. The instance's other
placements are not changed and read as behind: the config ladder reports the lowest rung across
the instance's live placements, so the instance reads as not converged until a fleet applies the
new generation to them (`submitFleetApply`, one member per placement).

**Agent placements** (plan 015 T3.3): a placement whose target's transport is `agent` answers `501 AGENT_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` (no agent applies a log-level generation in v1); nothing is staged.

**Permission:** `logs.setLevel`
**Scope:** `instance`

**Responses:**

- `202` — Accepted and durable.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `CONFLICT` — an apply or a stop is already in flight for this scope.
- `422` — `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `mode: live` on a direct-HTTP-only placement (`OR-43`: P2 only); `mode: config` for a package that declares no logger support; or an instance with no staged configuration to carry the level.
- `501` — `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` — `mode: live`, because no live write is built (`OR-103`); or `AGENT_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` — the placement's target is an agent (nothing was staged, no SSH connection was made).

**Restore the product defaults**

Row 66. Clears the hide overrides and the default placements, **keeps every shared widget**
(`OQ-8` (a)), and returns the dashboard as it now renders. Concurrency as `saveWidget`.

**Permission:** `dashboard.reset`
**Scope:** `instance`

**Responses:**

- `200` — The dashboard after the reset.
- `400` — The request failed validation.
- `401` — No session, or the session is expired or revoked.
- `403` — `FORBIDDEN`, `CSRF_REJECTED` or `ORIGIN_REJECTED` — switch on `code`. `FORBIDDEN` means the verb is not held at the resource's scope.
- `404` — ⚠️ **Deliberately indistinguishable from "exists but out of your scope".** Discriminating the two leaks existence across a scope boundary.
- `409` — `CONFLICT` — the dashboard's `revision` has moved since it was read.
- `503` — `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — retryable: a dependency did not answer. Not a credential outcome.

Auth: session cookie (`__Host-SM_SESSION`) from the login call plus the `X-SM-CSRF` header and a trusted `Origin` (both pre-filled).
